_comment: The prologue (docs/CASE_00_CASH_TIN.md 'Tutorial building steps'). Each step has a check the Prologue class evaluates against the game; they complete in order.

steps.title: Arrival
steps.text: A truck drops you at the siding. Agnes Doyle's cottage is the only building in the valley. You are the Administrator, and the Constable. Have a look round.
steps.hint: Drag to look around, scroll or pinch to zoom. Tap Continue when you're ready.

steps.title: Lay the main road
steps.text: A town needs a road. Lay one from the siding east past Agnes's cottage, following the ghost path.
steps.hint: Open Roads and follow the dotted path. Dirt roads are free, but they turn to mud in the rain.

steps.title: Build the general store
steps.text: The Haywards are coming to run the store, and the telephone exchange goes in the back room. Build it on the marked plot.
steps.hint: Use the store template or design your own. It needs a front door onto the road, a back window facing the creek for light in the storeroom, and an exchange room.

steps.title: Build three houses
steps.text: Three more families are waiting at the siding. Build three houses north of the road and furnish them.
steps.hint: Start from the cottage template, then make each house a home: beds, a table, somewhere to cook.

steps.title: Approve the families
steps.text: Choose which house each family gets. The Haywards are already set for the store.
steps.hint: Open Residents (P) and offer each family a house.

steps.title: The first week
steps.text: Let the week run. Watch what people do, who they visit and what they want. On Saturday the town holds its welcome dance in the mill shed.
steps.hint: Click a resident to see their card. Speed up time with the clock buttons.

steps.title: Something's wrong
steps.text: The Haywards have come home from the dance to find the back window open and the cash tin gone.
steps.hint: Search the scene, speak to everyone, and find out who did it.

steps.title: The Cash Tin
steps.text: Search the store, gather the records, interview the residents, and make your accusation.
steps.hint: Present evidence that contradicts what people say. Link your deductions. A wrong accusation costs Town Trust.

steps.title: A lesson learned
steps.text: Residents have started latching their windows. A lamp behind the store wouldn't hurt either. Footpaths and street lamps are now yours to build.
steps.hint: Prevention is part of play. The town is yours now.
